D.t: Charles Booker trails by 14.1 and wins 2% of simulations. Closing it takes about 117,054 voters switching sides, or 234,107 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +22.6 and R +5.3. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Jefferson, a projected net 114,341 votes; Fayette, a projected net 44,027 votes; Franklin, a projected net 3,854 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Kenton, R +9.8, 3.7% of the vote; Warren, R +11.6, 2.7% of the vote; Campbell, R +6.9, 2.2% of the vote; Hardin, R +11.3, 2.2% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Charles Booker runs furthest behind in Boone, Laurel, Oldham. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 40 to 60, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.51 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 69% of voters, 42 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.44 points; Voters without a degree, 67% of voters, 40 to 60, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.37 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Charles Booker: Immigration voters 18 to 82, Small counties 31 to 69, 2024 voters who skipped 2022 38 to 62. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$310K cash against $2.3M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Registered Democrats cast 57% of the 38,664 ballots in Kentucky so far, against 42% for the other party. That is 2.2 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.
